scenarios.name: credential_access_comsvcs
scenarios.description: Real capture: rundll32.exe (child of a PowerShell process) invokes comsvcs.dll,MiniDump against lsass.exe, writing a dump file. Command line: "C:\Windows\System32\rundll32.exe" C:\windows\System32\comsvcs.dll MiniDump 756 C:\Users\wardog\AppData\Local\Temp\lsass-comsvcs.dmp full
scenarios.alert: Alert on WORKSTATION5: process rundll32.exe. Review this process and its related activity.

scenarios.name: persistence_run_key
scenarios.description: Real capture: powershell.exe writes HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\Updater, whose value is itself a second-stage encoded PowerShell launcher read back out of a registry value (fileless persistence): Details="...powershell.exe" -c "$x=$((gp HKLM:SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion Debug).Debug);powershell -Win Hidden -enc $x"
scenarios.alert: Alert on WORKSTATION5.mordor.local: process powershell.exe. Review this process and its related activity.
scenarios.caveat: OTRF's recording of this technique starts after the actor process was already running, so the source file has no Sysmon EventID=1 (process-create) for this ProcessGuid - only its registry writes (19x) and network activity. One technique with nothing else to corroborate it is labelled SUSPICIOUS, not MALICIOUS.
